Several instances of a Node application acting as one, through Redis. It is the counterpart of the Java `egradx-redis`. It uses the same keys, channels and messages (`contracts/redis`), so Node, Java and Python instances behind one Redis count, evict and push together. The client is the official [`redis`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/redis) (node-redis).

| What | Without it (one instance) | With it |
|---|---|---|
| Wrong passwords (egradx-auth's limiter) | each instance counts its own | counted together, in two sorted sets per guess |
| A change to a role's authorities | other instances see it when their cache entry expires (60 s) | every instance evicts it at once |
| An in-app notification's live push | only the streams open on the instance that published it | the streams open on every instance |

```ts
import { createRedisCoordination } from '@babulvaibhav/egradx-redis';

const redis = createRedisCoordination({ url: process.env.REDIS_URL });   // or { client } — a node-redis client of the application's
const egradx = createEgradx({ prisma, auth: { … }, redis });             // @babulvaibhav/egradx-sdk wires, starts and closes it
await egradx.start();
```

Without the umbrella, wire each piece yourself:

```ts
const auth = createAuth({ …, limiter: redis.attemptLimiter });
const notifications = createNotifications({ …, broadcaster: redis.broadcaster });
redis.connect({ auth, notifications });
await redis.start();
// …
await redis.close();
```

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `createRedisCoordination({ client \| url, keyPrefix?, enabled?, commandTimeoutMs?, subscribeRetryMs?, log?, metrics? })` | Everything below. `keyPrefix` (default `egradx:`) starts every key and channel: instances that act together use the same one, applications sharing a Redis use different ones. `enabled: false` (Java's `egradx.redis.enabled`) counts in memory and pushes on this instance only, with no Redis at all. A client given is the application's to connect and close; one made from `url` is connected by `start()` and closed by `close()`. |
| `attemptLimiter` | egradx-auth's `limiter`: a factory auth calls with its `rateLimit` settings (and does not call when `rateLimit.enabled` is false), so Redis counts with the same limits and window. Call it with settings for a limiter on its own (`EgradxRedisAttemptLimiter`). |
| `broadcaster` | egradx-notification's `broadcaster`: publishes each in-app notification on `<prefix>notification:published`; every instance, this one included, hands what it receives to its own `deliverLocally`. |
| `connect({ auth?, notifications? })` | Once the libraries exist: a role change that commits on this instance (`auth.roles.onAuthoritiesChanged`) is published on `<prefix>auth:role-authorities-changed`, and every instance evicts it (`auth.roles.evictAuthorities`); received notifications go to `notifications.deliverLocally`. |
| `start()`, `isSubscribed()`, `close()` | The subscriptions run on a connection of their own (`client.duplicate()`), started in the background: `start()` never fails or waits for Redis. While Redis is down they try again every `subscribeRetryMs` (5 s, as Java); once subscribed, node-redis reconnects and resubscribes on its own. |
| `EgradxRedisMessages` | The channel names, and reading and writing the messages of `contracts/redis/messages.json`. A reader ignores fields it does not know; a message it cannot read is dropped and logged. |
| `EgradxRedisFailures` | Counts every failure (`egradx.redis.failures`, tagged `operation`: `auth.attempts`, `auth.role-authorities-changed`, `notification.published`, `subscribe`) and logs it at most once a minute per operation. |

## When Redis is unavailable

Nothing fails because Redis does (contracts/redis). Sign-in is allowed and failures are not counted; other instances' caches expire a changed role within their TTL; a notification is pushed on this instance only. A command fails at once while the client has no connection (node-redis would otherwise queue it until there is one) and after `commandTimeoutMs` (2 s) when Redis does not answer, so a sign-in never waits longer than that on Redis. node-redis reports every connection failure as an `'error'` event, which ends a process that has no listener for it; this package listens on the client it is given, as well as on its own.

## Tests

- `contract.test.ts`: every message of `contracts/redis/messages.json` read and written back equal (timestamps as instants); unknown fields ignored, unreadable messages refused.
- `fail-open.test.ts`: against nothing (port 1), start does not wait or throw, the limiter allows and counts its failures, a notification is pushed locally, a role change is evicted locally, and subscribing keeps retrying.
- `instances.test.ts`, with `EGRADX_TEST_REDIS_URL` (e.g. `redis://localhost:6379`): two instances count, wait and clear together; the keys, members, scores and expiry are exactly the contract's, and a set written as another SDK writes it is counted; a role change reaches the other instance; a notification is pushed once on each.

## Classes

### EgradxRedisAttemptLimiter

Counts wrong passwords in Redis, so every instance counts together: the same sliding window, limits and waits as
egradx-auth's EgradxInMemoryAttemptLimiter, kept in two sorted sets per guess (contracts/redis). As Java's
EgradxRedisAttemptLimiter, command for command.

Fails open: while Redis is unavailable, sign-in is allowed and failures go uncounted, as without a limiter at all.

### EgradxRedisFailures

What happens when Redis fails: nothing fails with it. Each failure is counted (`egradx.redis.failures`, tagged
`operation`) and logged, at most once a minute per operation, so an outage is visible without flooding the log; the
caller then carries on as a single instance would (contracts/redis). As Java's EgradxRedisFailures.

### RedisCoordinationOptions

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| <a id="property-client"></a> `client?` | [`EgradxRedisClient`](#egradxredisclient) | The Redis server: a node-redis client (`createClient()` from `redis`), which the application connects and closes, or a URL (`redis://localhost:6379`), for a client this creates, connects in `start()` and closes in `close()`. |
| <a id="property-commandtimeoutms"></a> `commandTimeoutMs?` | `number` | How long a command may take before it counts as failed and the caller carries on without Redis. Default 2000 ms. |
| <a id="property-enabled"></a> `enabled?` | `boolean` | Whether the libraries coordinate through Redis (Java: egradx.redis.enabled). Off, each instance counts, caches and pushes on its own. Default true. |
| <a id="property-keyprefix"></a> `keyPrefix?` | `string` | Starts every key and channel (Java: egradx.redis.key-prefix). Instances that must act together use the same prefix; applications sharing one Redis use different ones. Default `egradx:`. |
| <a id="property-log"></a> `log?` | [`EgradxRedisLog`](#egradxredislog) | Default: the console. |
| <a id="property-metrics"></a> `metrics?` | [`EgradxMetrics`](/docs/reference/node/egradx-sdk#egradxmetrics) | Counts `egradx.redis.failures` (tagged `operation`). Default the global meter provider. |
| <a id="property-subscriberetryms"></a> `subscribeRetryMs?` | `number` | How often the subscriptions try again while Redis is down (Java: every 5 s). Default 5000 ms. |
| <a id="property-url"></a> `url?` | `string` | - |

## Functions

### createRedisCoordination()

```ts
function createRedisCoordination(options?): RedisCoordination;
```

Makes several instances of an application act as one, through Redis, as Java's egradx-redis does when added: the
attempt limiter counts in Redis, role changes are relayed to every instance's cache, and in-app notifications are
pushed live on every instance (contracts/redis). Every Redis failure is counted and logged, and the instance carries on
as if it were alone.

  const redis = createRedisCoordination({ url: process.env.REDIS_URL });
  const auth = createAuth({ …, limiter: redis.attemptLimiter });
  const notifications = createNotifications({ …, broadcaster: redis.broadcaster });
  redis.connect({ auth, notifications });
  await redis.start();

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options` | [`RedisCoordinationOptions`](#rediscoordinationoptions) |

#### Returns

[`RedisCoordination`](#rediscoordination)
